study.title: Accelerating crystal structure search through active learning with neural networks for rapid relaxations
study.citation: Hessmann SSP et al. npj Computational Materials 11, 44 (2025).
study.workflow_type: Active-learning crystal structure search with random structure generation, ensemble force-field relaxation, and DFT labelling
study.assessment_scope: Published article, Supplementary Information, data and code availability statements, linked data and code records, and released configuration files; the analysis was not rerun. Converted to version 1.0.0 identifiers from the version 0.2.0 audit of 2026-07-20.

items.summary: The initial and final candidate pools, acquired training structures, DFT-validated structures, and final ensembles are deposited, and the linked DepositOnce data record identifies a CC BY 4.0 licence. Candidate-generation constraints are stated, but stable item hashes and a duplicate rule with cross-split collision rate are not reported.
source_locations: main text, "Initial structure generation" and Methods, "Constraints for initial structure generation"

items.summary: A 20% validation split is used to monitor ensemble training. The grouping strategy, split manifest, random seeds, and an independent test-set protocol are not stated.

The five-model SO(3)-equivariant ensemble is defined with two interaction layers, 64 features, lmax=2, and a 7 Å cutoff. The input crystal representation is described, but random seeds are not provided.

Adam optimisation, batch size 10, an initial learning rate of 0.0005, validation-based scheduling, loss weights, and device allocation are reported. Epoch counts, numerical precision, and wall-clock uncertainty for training are not all provided.

The proposal engine is random and symmetry-constrained structure generation rather than a trained generative model. Random and symmetry-constrained candidate generation, minimum interatomic distances, lattice bounds, pool sizes, rejection rules, clustering, machine-learning relaxation, and final DFT relaxation are specified.
source_locations: main text, "Initial structure generation" through "Structure relaxation"

items.summary: DFT evaluations required to recover low-energy structures, relaxation outcomes, and mean and standard deviation over three simulations per composition are reported. General validity, novelty, and diversity definitions are not part of the evaluation.
source_locations: Results, "Global energy minimum", Fig. 3, and "Multiple low-energy structures", Fig. 4

items.summary: Machine-learning relaxations are escalated to DFT under a pinned Quantum ESPRESSO, PAW, PBE, pseudopotential, cutoff, k-point, force-convergence, and timeout protocol. This establishes low-energy structures under the stated calculation settings; the study does not make or validate route-specific synthesizability claims.

The workflow is compared with random search, Bayesian optimisation, and learning-accelerated local search. The authors explicitly note that the baselines stop once the target is found whereas the proposed method runs to its own convergence criterion, so the baseline evaluation counts are optimistic lower bounds.

The acquisition score combines predicted energy and maximum force magnitude, while ensemble force uncertainty determines when each machine-learning relaxation is stopped. The per-cycle DFT batch varies from 100 to 200 structures; five models supply uncertainty; stopping tracks stabilisation of the k lowest-energy clusters over a stated number of cycles and energy tolerance; and total DFT counts and three independent simulations per composition are reported.
source_locations: main text, "Collecting training data", "Structure relaxation", and "Stopping criterion"
code configuration, src/scripts/configs/main.yaml and experiment configurations

items.summary: Candidate pools, acquired labels, final ensembles, configurations, installation instructions, and code are archived with repository and Zenodo or DepositOnce records. An environment lockfile, split checksums, one-command figure rebuild, and complete determinism statement are not identified.

The runtime analysis separates DFT labelling, ensemble training, machine-learning relaxation, and DFT validation. DFT uses 16 CPU cores, whereas training and prediction use one GPU and four CPU cores; approximately 90% of CPU core-hours are attributed to DFT labelling. Energy and carbon estimates, candidates per GPU-hour, and associated uncertainty are not reported.
source_locations: Supplementary Section B and Supplementary Fig. 2

items.summary: The workflow searches low-energy structures for three stated inorganic compositions and does not expose a hazardous target, autonomous execution pathway, or access mechanism that makes a governance control material to the claim. Data and code licences are assessed under Data and Reproducibility.
source_locations: main article, "Initial structure generation", Data availability, and Code availability

items.summary: The number of DFT labels, per-cycle batch size, ensemble size, simulation replicates, validation relaxations, and device allocation can be reconstructed, but they are not consolidated with the full candidate attrition and compute footprint in one record.
